observation: The qualification engine loads exactly all125 decisions, all28 requirement groups and all97 candidate contracts, validates individually fingerprinted closure reviews and actual completed-suite cases, and records every missing local/native acceptance independently. It refuses count-based completion and keeps full scope visible.
executed_case_references: tests/qualification-tools.test.mjs:13 — ADR-120: complete-scope evidence refuses stale, fabricated, file-only, skipped and unreviewed scenario claims

scenario: Modify stable event contract after publication
expected_behavior: Version bump/migration checks required, UI-only change may stay internal
observation: Canonical Event v1 matches the proposed schema and its pinned version fingerprint; changed descriptors and unsupported event versions require explicit compatibility/migration handling. UI source is outside this contract descriptor. General dependency-cache invalidation remains separately partial under ADR-078.
executed_case_references: tests/versioned-canonical-events.test.mjs:23 — ADR-121: stable canonical descriptor matches the proposed Event schema and its published version fingerprint;tests/versioned-canonical-events.test.mjs:48 — unknown event versions and incomplete causal envelopes are rejected before persistence;tests/node-extensions.test.mjs:30 — extension contract enforces version, declared ports, shape and no arbitrary effects

scenario: Review one decision against requirement, contract and test
expected_behavior: Bidirectional traceability exists and contradictions are explicitly logged
observation: The trace engine links each authoritative decision, requirement, named contract, candidate contract, actual implementation and case in both directions. It checks missing inverse mappings, scenario-ID/domain contradictions, missing semantic descriptions, unavailable nodes/services, and records explicit service/interface deviations rather than candidate-ID equality.
executed_case_references: tests/qualification-tools.test.mjs:14 — ADR-122: normative traceability is bidirectional and reports contradictory requirements, scenarios and semantic aliases

scenario: Merge concurrent batch implementing two dependent features
expected_behavior: Incremental integration gates run; shared contracts owned and versioned
observation: Dependent changes are integrated in one checkout with failing-before/passing-after regressions; batch counts are not used as acceptance evidence.
executed_case_references: tests/canonical-domain-integration.test.mjs:35 — ADR-031: approved objective graph effect feeds the canonical quest publication service

scenario: Advertise Foundry compatibility for untested build
expected_behavior: Release matrix declines unsupported claim without passing evidence
observation: The release matrix declines compatibility without current exact source/version, real native environment identity, artifact fingerprints, all125 executed scenarios, all required native dimensions and functional/semantic closure. It rejects mocks, future timestamps, stale artifacts, missing system versions and failed or blocked native evidence.
executed_case_references: tests/qualification-tools.test.mjs:15 — ADR-124: native compatibility requires exact executed build/system evidence and declines unsupported release claims

scenario: Propose new external server after architecture closure
expected_behavior: Change rejected pending explicit amendment; full module single-deliverable scope retained
observation: The runtime remains one native Foundry module with no mandatory external backend or database; developer tooling is outside the installable artifact.
